producer.provenance: captured PyTorch with deliberate logging fault

findings.title: Non-finite training loss
findings.message: train/loss became NaN at step 60 (20 non-finite point(s) in this run).
fixes: Inspect the objective and logging reduction separately: an empty batch or empty logging window can produce NaN even while optimizer updates remain finite.
Check for a divide-by-zero or log(0) in the loss calculation.
If the optimizer's loss or gradients also become non-finite, inspect the learning rate, gradient clipping and mixed-precision loss scaling.

finite-control.provenance: synthetic boundary/control fixture generated by replay.py

findings.title: Setback
findings.message: train/loss left a level of 1 at step 60, rose to 4, and was back by step 80: 20 steps (17% of the run) above a level it had already reached, with 75% of the run's progress given back at the worst point.
fixes: Look at what changed at the first step: the learning rate, a new data shard, an epoch boundary.
Lower the peak learning rate or clip gradients if the rise follows a large update.
If this was a planned restart or curriculum stage, it is expected.

findings.title: Loss rose within final finite segment
findings.message: Within the final finite segment, train/loss started around 3.07 and ended at 6.36, 2.1x higher, without ever settling below its first level. Assessed within the finite segment at steps 50-99 (50 observations); no loss trajectory is inferred across NaN/Inf readings.
fixes: Lower the learning rate; a loss that climbs from the first step is usually an LR an order of magnitude too high.
Add LR warmup and gradient clipping.
Check the loss is the quantity being minimized (sign, reduction, label alignment).
